classes.name: Estrogen — transdermal
classes.description: Transdermal 17β-estradiol (patch, gel, or spray); skips first-pass hepatic metabolism, lower VTE risk than oral.
classes.plainDescription: An estrogen patch or gel absorbed through the skin — gentler on clot risk than pills.

classes.name: Estrogen — oral
classes.description: Oral estradiol or conjugated estrogens; effective, but first-pass hepatic metabolism raises VTE/clot and stroke risk vs transdermal.
classes.plainDescription: An estrogen pill taken by mouth. Works well, but carries a higher clot risk than the patch.

classes.name: Progestogen
classes.description: Progestogen added to systemic estrogen for endometrial protection in patients with an intact uterus; micronized progesterone preferred.
classes.plainDescription: Added to estrogen if you still have a uterus, to protect the uterine lining.

classes.name: Vaginal (local) estrogen
classes.description: Low-dose vaginal estradiol (cream, tablet, insert, or ring) for genitourinary syndrome of menopause; minimal systemic absorption.
classes.plainDescription: Low-dose estrogen placed vaginally for dryness and urinary symptoms (GSM).

classes.name: Estrogen–progestin (oral combo)
classes.description: A single oral tablet with both an estrogen and a progestin, for a person with an intact uterus; generic estradiol/norethindrone acetate is the usual first-pass.
classes.plainDescription: One pill that combines estrogen and the uterus-protecting hormone.

records.verificationNote: Read page 63: estradiol 0.025 to 0.1 mg/24 hr weekly patch, Tier 4, QL 4 per 28 days, no PA/ST; 0.05 mg/24 hr is in the strength list. Semiweekly patches on pages 62, 63 and 65 are alternatives. No estradiol gel or spray appears on the list, so the class description's gel/spray forms are not covered as a finding. The strength chosen is a pick from the listed range, not a documented preference; sig is standard label dosing.

records.verificationNote: Read page 63: estradiol 0.5, 1 and 2 mg tablet, Tier 1, Mail Order, no UM requirement. Estradiol 1 mg picked as the lowest-tier, no-restriction strength. Premarin, generic conjugated estrogens, Menest on pages 62, 65, 66 are covered at Tier 4 without UM. DUAVEE (page 62) carries PA and is listed as a barrier. Estradiol-norethindrone combos are on page 63 and are handled in the combo class.

records.verificationNote: Read page 66: progesterone micronized 100 mg and 200 mg capsules, Tier 3, no UM; 100 mg insert, Tier 4. Judgment call: medroxyprogesterone 2.5/5/10 mg (page 65) is Tier 2, which is cheaper than Tier 3. Micronized progesterone is kept as the pick because the class definition names it as the preferred progestogen. Sig is standard label dosing. Route for the insert is not printed on the line.

The formulary line does not print the route; the cream is identified by strength and dosage form, and vaginal use is the standard labeling for this product, so the route is inferred from labeling. Premarin vaginal cream (page 66) is Tier 3. The 10 mcg tablet is the vaginal insert form per standard labeling (route not printed).
